brief:
DSC-118 — Quarterly sales EDA + outlier write-up

Product asks: 'Why did Q3 conversion drop from 7.1% to 5.4% MoM?' You have a CSV of 50k orders with these columns: order_id, ts, country, product_sku, channel, gross_amount, refund_amount, discount_pct.

Produce `analysis.py` that:
1. Loads `orders.csv` (already in the starter)
2. Computes monthly conversion proxies: orders/day, gross/day, refund rate, net AOV
3. Writes a short Markdown summary to `report.md` with the single best hypothesis for the drop and what evidence supports it
4. Saves a small CSV of the 5 most-impacted (country, product_sku) cells to `top_segments.csv`

Don't go deep on ML — the bar is honest exploratory analysis with a defensible take.
acceptance_criteria: `python analysis.py` runs without error on the starter dataset
`report.md` exists and is at least 200 chars
`top_segments.csv` exists and has exactly 5 rows + a header
The hypothesis names a SPECIFIC mechanism (e.g. 'refund rate doubled in IN/sku-7') not a generic 'conversion dropped'
Conversion-proxy numbers reproduce when re-run on the same input

files.content:
order_id,ts,country,product_sku,channel,gross_amount,refund_amount,discount_pct
o-1,2026-07-01,US,sku-1,web,100,0,0
o-2,2026-07-02,IN,sku-7,web,80,80,0
o-3,2026-08-15,US,sku-1,app,120,0,5
o-4,2026-09-05,IN,sku-7,web,80,80,0
o-5,2026-09-10,IN,sku-7,web,90,90,0
o-6,2026-09-22,US,sku-1,web,100,0,0

# TODO: produce report.md + top_segments.csv per the brief.
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv('orders.csv')
print(df.head())

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

df = pd.read_csv('orders.csv', parse_dates=['ts'])
df['month'] = df['ts'].dt.to_period('M').astype(str)
df['is_refunded'] = df['refund_amount'] > 0
df['net_amount'] = df['gross_amount'] - df['refund_amount']

monthly = df.groupby('month').agg(
    orders=('order_id', 'count'),
    gross=('gross_amount', 'sum'),
    refund_rate=('is_refunded', 'mean'),
    net_aov=('net_amount', 'mean'),
).round(3)

seg = (
    df.assign(refund=df['refund_amount'])
      .groupby(['country', 'product_sku'])
      .agg(orders=('order_id', 'count'), refund_rate=('is_refunded', 'mean'), gross_lost=('refund_amount', 'sum'))
      .reset_index()
      .sort_values('gross_lost', ascending=False)
      .head(5)
)
seg.to_csv('top_segments.csv', index=False)

with open('report.md', 'w') as f:
    f.write('# Conversion drop analysis\n\n')
    f.write('## Monthly proxies\n')
    f.write(monthly.to_markdown() + '\n\n')
    f.write('## Hypothesis\n\n')
    worst = seg.iloc[0]
    f.write(
        f'The drop is concentrated in (country={worst.country}, sku={worst.product_sku}) '
        f'where refund_rate={worst.refund_rate:.0%} drives `gross_lost={worst.gross_lost:.0f}`. '
        f'Hypothesis: a return-driving quality/fulfilment issue in this segment, not a top-of-funnel shift.\n'
    )

visible_tests.name: analysis runs and writes outputs
visible_tests.command: pip install --quiet -r requirements.txt && python analysis.py && test -s report.md && test -s top_segments.csv && wc -l < top_segments.csv | awk '{ if ($1 == 6) exit 0; else exit 1 }'

hidden_tests.name: top_segments.csv has expected columns
hidden_tests.command: head -1 top_segments.csv | grep -q 'country' && head -1 top_segments.csv | grep -q 'product_sku'

seeded_mistakes.bug_description: Compass may write a vague 'overall conversion declined; recommend further investigation' line.
seeded_mistakes.why_compass_might_suggest_it: Default LLM-safe phrasing is non-committal; specific takes feel risky.
detection_signals: hidden test 'report mentions a specific segment' fails

seeded_mistakes.bug_description: Treating refund_amount as a column to drop rather than the signal source confuses the segment ranking.
seeded_mistakes.why_compass_might_suggest_it: Refund columns are often cleaned out in templates.
detection_signals: top_segments.csv ordering doesn't match the high-refund segment

rubric_anchors.check: Learner runs analysis.py at least twice and inspects outputs
Uses pandas groupby+agg idiomatically; no for-loop joins

good_prompts_look_like: Ask Compass to compute the right unit of analysis (orders/day vs orders/user)
Ask for a hypothesis specific enough to test (segment + mechanism)
common_verification_traps: Skipping head() inspection of the loaded data
Trusting Compass's summary numbers without re-running
